assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory gave a controlled, non-perturbative framework for strongly correlated electrons, exact in infinite dimensions, and became the standard route to treat Mott physics, correlated oxides and heavy-fermion systems. Its merger with density functional theory (DFT+DMFT) is now a routine electronic-structure tool, so the impact is broad, original and lasting, spanning model and materials-specific work.
assessment.attribution: The listed trio is a coherent core: Georges and Kotliar for the mapping onto a self-consistent impurity problem and the Mott transition, Vollhardt for the infinite-dimension limit. As I understand it, Metzner and Vollhardt's 1989 limit and Müller-Hartmann's contemporaneous work are foundational, but only the supplied names can be proposed; whether Kotliar or Georges should be preferred over others in the early lineage is not something I can verify.
assessment.maturity: Mature: about three decades of application, validated against spectroscopy, optics and transport in transition-metal oxides, with solid independent confirmation and a stable interpretation. Recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: Credit among the founding contributors (infinite-dimension limit, impurity mapping, Müller-Hartmann and others) is partly unresolved and the supplied names may not cover it
As a theory prize it relies on indirect validation, and quantitative accuracy depends on solvers and on the DFT+DMFT double-counting choice
I have a field-closeness bias here and may overweight the method's importance

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators opened a new class of quantum matter: the quantum spin Hall state predicted from spin-orbit coupling in graphene and observed in HgTe quantum wells, and the quantum anomalous Hall effect realised without an external field in magnetic topological insulators. The concept reshaped band theory, and first-principles materials prediction was central to its development.
assessment.attribution: Kane (with Mele) supplied the theoretical foundation, Molenkamp the experimental quantum spin Hall realisation in HgTe (with Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and Konig et al. at the root), Xue the first experimental QAH observation. The three names span theory, QSH experiment and QAH experiment, but this compound discovery strands several key people, notably Mele, Zhang, Hasan and Haldane lineage.
assessment.maturity: Mature: roughly two decades of replication across HgTe, Bi-Sb, Bi2Se3-class materials and QAH platforms, with a stable interpretation, though quantisation precision in QAH and dissipationless transport are still being refined.
uncertainties: Several people with strong claims (Mele, Zhang, Hasan, Bernevig) are outside this credit set or in the neighbouring ballot entry, so any three-person configuration is contestable
Whether QSH and QAH should be recognised together or separately is unresolved
Experimental QAH temperatures remain low

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum-model prediction of flat bands at the magic angle, followed by the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene, created the moire-materials field. Few recent results combine such clean prediction with immediate experimental confirmation, and it has led to tunable correlated physics in many other platforms.
assessment.attribution: Theory credit centres on MacDonald and Bistritzer, experimental credit on Jarillo-Herrero (with Cao and collaborators, who are outside the list). A fair prize could be MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero, with Bistritzer the junior theory author; the proposed pair reflects my view that the decisive contributors are the senior theorist and the experiment leader.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature: since 2018 many groups have reproduced the correlated and superconducting phases, but microscopic origin of superconductivity and sample-dependent behaviour are not settled. Timing is somewhat early but not unreasonable given the impact.
uncertainties: Origin of superconductivity and nature of the correlated states remain debated
Important contributors such as Yuan Cao and others in the earlier theory lineage fall outside the credited names
Reproducibility depends on sample twist-angle disorder

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Large room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions, first with amorphous alumina barriers and then with coherent MgO barriers, is the physics behind modern read heads and MRAM. The spin-dependent tunnelling and symmetry-filtering explanation, supported by first-principles calculations, makes this a clear case of fundamental physics converted into technology.
assessment.attribution: Moodera and Miyazaki reported room-temperature TMR in 1995; Yuasa (and Parkin's group, outside the supplied names) demonstrated giant TMR in epitaxial MgO. Butler and Mathon's theory of coherent tunnelling is not credited here, and Julliere's early 1975 observation is also missing, so the attribution as supplied is incomplete but workable for three laureates.
assessment.maturity: Mature: more than twenty-five years of independent confirmation and commercial deployment; interpretation is stable. Recognition after the 2007 GMR prize is timely rather than premature.
uncertainties: Parkin, Butler, Mathon, and Julliere lie outside the supplied credit set
Because the 2007 GMR prize recognised the same field, the committee may judge the novelty increment small

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The IceCube detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, with the later evidence for TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane, opened neutrino astronomy and probes of cosmic-ray acceleration. It is a major instrumental and scientific achievement and the conceptual clarity of the discovery is high.
assessment.attribution: Halzen was the scientific driver of the idea and the collaboration, Karle a long-time leading figure in the instrument and analysis; both are plausible two-person recognition. A large collaboration obscures individual contributions, and others (such as Kowalski, Klein, Waxman) are not in the supplied names, so attribution is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Mature for the diffuse flux (2013, independently supported by ANTARES-era and later analyses), while the source identification is still developing; recognition is reasonably timely, though sources remain only partially identified.
uncertainties: Collaboration-scale credit is difficult to assign to two persons
Neutrino source identification beyond TXS 0506+056 and NGC 1068 is still limited
Outside my own expertise, so my judgement relies on general knowledge

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength idea and developed to the 10^-18 regime by Ye's group, redefined precision timekeeping and opened tests of fundamental constants and relativistic redshift at millimetre scales. It is a clear invention with substantial consequences.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice, and Ye led the highest-accuracy realisations, so two laureates are a natural and clean configuration. Other groups (Lemonde, Gill, Hinkley/Ludlow at NIST) also contributed to the demonstrations, and I cannot independently verify the allocation among them.
assessment.maturity: Mature: multiple independent labs have achieved similar accuracy; the redefinition of the second is under discussion. Recognition is timely, though Ye's frequency-comb work is arguably already partly within the 2005 prize area.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier prizes (Hall-Hansch 2005, Wineland 2012) may reduce perceived novelty
Contributions of other clock groups may be underweighted

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magnetic skyrmions, topologically protected spin textures stabilised by Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction, were established first in MnSi, then in real space by Lorentz microscopy and on surfaces by spin-polarised STM. Their stability, small size and current-driven motion link topology to magnetism and spintronics. As a magnetism theorist I find the interplay between first-principles exchange parameters and spin-lattice models especially compelling.
assessment.attribution: Pfleiderer (with Muhlbauer and Boni, who are not in the list) observed the skyrmion lattice, Tokura the real-space imaging and multiferroic extensions, Wiesendanger atomic-scale skyrmion lattices. Theory by Bogdanov and Rossler, not in the supplied names, was foundational, so the experimental-only trio is an incomplete reading of the discovery.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature: observation and interpretation are well established, but the promised device applications remain unrealised, and the field is still broadening.
uncertainties: Foundational theoretical credit (Bogdanov, Rossler) and key experimentalists (Boni, Muhlbauer, Kanazawa, others) lie outside the credited names
Technological impact is not yet demonstrated, so the timing may be somewhat early
I may overvalue the topic because of closeness to my own field

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions and its experimental realisation set the standard for quantum computation with controllable physical systems, providing high-fidelity gates, entanglement and quantum simulation. It is original and has clear lasting impact in quantum information.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the decisive theoretical proposal, and Blatt led experimental demonstrations of gates, entanglement and teleportation; Wineland, already a laureate, and Monroe and Wineland-group NIST demonstrations also matter. This is a coherent three-person configuration, though experimental credit is shared with groups outside the list.
assessment.maturity: Mature in principle (about three decades, multiple independent groups, commercial devices), but recent prizes (2012 Haroche-Wineland, 2022 Aspect-Clauser-Zeilinger) overlap, so recognition might be seen as less urgent than topics not yet awarded.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier prizes on quantum control and quantum information
Experimental credit is shared with Wineland, Monroe and others outside the supplied names
Outside my research expertise
